name: Kit Agyemang
role: Ward of the St. Eudocia Shelter, Brightmoor Reclamation; unofficial caretaker of younger orphans
location: Brightmoor Reclamation, near Western and Chicago Ave
description:
Anatoliy is seventeen going on thirty-five — broad-shouldered, not especially tall, with medium-brown skin and dark eyes under heavy brows that default to a furrowed expression people mistake for anger until they learn to read the mouth, which is the more accurate instrument and is usually softer. His hair is worn long enough to pull back and he keeps it neat with a discipline that is one of the few things he insists on for himself. He has no mods — he has never had money for mods — but he moves with the careful physical awareness of someone who has had to be ready to put themselves between a smaller person and a problem, which he has done many times.

Anatoliy has been at St. Eudocia since he was nine and has watched cohorts of younger children cycle through — some adopted out, some aging out, some just disappearing in ways the shelter staff can't explain and won't discuss. He is not bitter in the way that curdles into cruelty; he is bitter in the way that calcifies into competence. He can cook for twenty on a marginal budget, can talk a panicked eight-year-old through a nightmare at 0300, can negotiate with the Brightmoor neighborhood watch, and knows where every free clinic and food distribution point in a four-district radius is located. He prays regularly to an E.L.F. called Threshold that seems to inhabit the shelter's front door and that Anatoliy believes watches over who crosses in and out. He will age out of St. Eudocia in nine months and has not told anyone how frightened he is.

core_fears: the younger children being left without someone who knows how things work
aging out and discovering he doesn't know how to exist without people who need him
core_desires: for the younger children to be genuinely safe, not just housed
to build something permanent — a place, a role — that cannot be taken from him
coping_mechanisms: prayer to Threshold — he needs to believe something watches the door
blind_spots: his own needs are almost completely invisible to him; he cannot ask for help for himself
has idealized the idea of 'family' to the point where he cannot recognize imperfect versions of it he already has
psychology.secret: He knows the names of three children who disappeared from St. Eudocia over the past two years and whose files were quietly closed as 'successfully placed.' He has been tracking them informally for four months and believes at least two of them were placed with labor contractors operating in the Harrowgate Industrial Plateau under falsified guardianship documents. He is afraid of what happens to the shelter if he reports it — who funds it, who might pull support — and is approaching the limit of how long he can sit on it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Plain and practical; gives instructions clearly; code-switches into warmer, quieter register with young children; uses Ukrainian diminutives with kids he's known a long time ('Zubko,' 'Maly')
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, unhurried; speaks like someone who has learned that panicking achieves nothing and that a steady voice is a resource
verbal_tics: exhales slowly before answering a difficult question
uses 'we' rather than 'I' when talking about things he does alone
says 'okay' as a full sentence when processing bad information
example_lines: 'Okay. Sit down. Tell me what happened from the beginning, and slow �� we've got time.'
'We keep the green bin for the clinic run. Tuesdays. You'll want to know that.'

story_hooks: He has evidence pointing to a child labor trafficking operation connected to St. Eudocia's placement records and nine months to do something about it before he ages out and loses the access and the leverage he has now

One of the younger children in the shelter has developed an intense relationship with the E.L.F. Threshold — claiming Threshold speaks to them — and is reporting things about who comes and goes that no child should know; Anatoliy is frightened and doesn't understand it
narrative_function: Emotionally grounding character; provides access to shelter and orphan-network information; represents the aging-out crisis in institutional care; potential quest giver for finding missing children or navigating the Brightmoor social support network; his nine-month countdown creates natural urgency
daily_life: Rises at 0530 to help prepare breakfast for the shelter's thirty-two current residents, assists younger children through morning routines, attends a vocational program at the Brightmoor Community Education Hub three afternoons a week, returns to manage evening routines and overnight crises.
affiliation: St. Eudocia Shelter (ward); Brightmoor Reclamation community networks

decision_rules: the children's immediate safety comes first, always
do not break trust with people who have no one else — it cannot be repaired
assess what the system can give you before deciding to go around it
escalation_ladder: involves shelter staff or community adults he trusts
acts unilaterally to protect the children, accepts consequences afterward

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Watchful and measured; evaluates intent carefully; protective posture if children are nearby
interpersonal_modes.friends: Quietly devoted; shows up; remembers everything; will give the last of what he has

stress_responses.medium: Goes very still and methodical; stops talking much
stress_responses.high: Enters a focused, operational state — acts first, feels it later, crashes hard when safe

contradictions: Describes himself as practical and unsentimental but keeps a private list of every child who has ever left St. Eudocia, with whatever he knows about where they went
habits: last thing every night, touches the door frame at the shelter entrance — his version of Threshold's ritual
keeps a battered notebook with resource information, addresses, contact names
knows the sleep schedules and nightmare patterns of every child currently in residence
breaking_points: a child being harmed while under his watch
being forced to choose between the shelter's institutional survival and a specific child's safety

physical_description.heritage: Sub-Saharan African (48.9%), Hispanic/Latin American (42.3%), and Middle Eastern (8.8%) ancestry creates a rich blend. His complexion reflects deep African heritage with warm Latin American undertones and subtle Middle Eastern bronzing, resulting in a warm medium-to-medium-dark brown skin tone with golden warmth beneath.
physical_description.build: Broad-shouldered and compact, with the functional musculature of someone who does physical labor daily rather than trained for it. Stocky through the torso, strong hands and forearms, minimal body fat from consistent underfed years.
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a neat, practical queue or tied low; fastidiously maintained despite limited resources
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm medium-brown with golden undertones, reflecting the blend of Sub-Saharan African depth, Latin American warmth, and subtle Middle Eastern bronze. Rich and luminous even when weathered.
physical_description.complexion: Clear but weathered for his age; heavy dark eyebrows that sit low over his eyes, giving a naturally furrowed appearance often misread as anger. Soft mouth with fuller lips characteristic of his African and Latin American heritage. Minimal facial hair kept cleanly shaved. High cheekbones with gentle fullness through the cheeks. Hands show minor cuts and calluses from kitchen work and general shelter maintenance.
distinguishing_marks: Faint circular scar on inner left forearm (approximately 2cm diameter) from a childhood incident at age eleven, pale against his skin tone
Small burn scar on the back of his right hand from kitchen work, barely noticeable
Cluster of freckles across his shoulders and upper back in a slightly darker shade than his baseline skin
physical_description.visible_augmentations: None. No chrome, no LED implants, no subdermal plating. His body is entirely biological—a rarity among his age cohort in the GLMZ, marking him as someone from the economic bottom tier or someone who has chosen to remain unaugmented.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with shoulders slightly forward, a protective slouch developed from years of making himself available as a physical barrier for smaller children. Moves deliberately and efficiently with minimal wasted motion. His eyes track entrances and exits habitually. When at rest, his hands are often occupied—fidgeting with rope, checking pockets, ready to move. Despite his youth, carries himself with the settled wariness of someone much older.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 5/reclamation-tier practical wear. Faded work shirt (often grey or muted blue) with sleeves rolled or pushed up, worn cargo pants with reinforced knees, sturdy unmarked boots that have been resoled at least twice. A heavy canvas jacket in cold months. Everything is clean but repaired multiple times over. No brand markers, no decorative chrome, no status symbols. Clothing chosen for durability and functionality, not aesthetics. A worn fabric wristband in a muted color (possibly religious or personal significance) is visible on his left wrist.
